Account Manager Social Calendar · all weeks kept here, nothing is removed
Rules: post 9:30-11:30am IST · company stays anonymous in the post body · job link ALWAYS goes in the first comment, never the post · reply to comments within the hour · every link verified live before publishing.
Built early. This week was generated on 6 Sep, before the Sep 1-7 week had finished running, at Amit’s request. Two consequences. There is no engagement panel on the Sep 1-7 archive yet, because nobody has posted it. And the role pool had barely moved: only 11 genuinely new roles had appeared in Airtable, so 29 of these 49 are roles the same KAM is posting during Sep 1-7, and 15 more ran in Aug 25-31. Ranking put the older repeats first to maximise the gap. Every repeated role was rewritten from scratch against last week’s post as an explicit anti-example, and the assertion script fails if any sentence is reused, so the copy is genuinely new even where the role is not. Rahul has no fresh roles at all; Pranav has one. Raghav and Kritika are out of the rotation this week, so the week is 49 posts. Every KAM now has their own graphic style; the template gained an eighth page, so Sujith and Pranav no longer share with Tanvi and Lavanya, and Supriya moves onto the blue-mountain style. The dead-page rate doubled: 62 of 111 job pages checked had gone dead, against 19 of 75 last week, which is why several books needed two and three top-up passes. Rahul’s live book fell from 6 roles to 3 and Pranav’s to 2, so both lean on older senior roles from their own books. One role was dropped for an implausible band (a ₹10-100 LPA customer support seat).
Voice: curious. Notices an odd detail in the role and follows it.
7 of the seven ran within the last two weeks. Tanvi’s book could not fill a fresh week once dead pages were removed, so the two-week no-repeat was relaxed rather than borrowing from another AM.

KAM-wise engagement, Tue 26 Aug to Mon 31 Aug

Read from each KAM’s public LinkedIn profile, then matched by hand to the plan day each post belongs to. The numbers also sit on the individual cards below. Kritika and Raghav are excluded throughout: neither has ever logged a post URL, so no profile could be resolved and their 14 slots are unverified rather than zero. The denominator is 49, not 63.

KAMPlannedPostedDays coveredReactionsCommentsAvg / postBest post
Tanvi7442997.224
Rahul73259619.740
Lavanya711717.07
Supriya733173757.777
Priya7551062.03
Sujith7544054481.0320
Pranav755993319.891
Total49262478210630.1320

26 posts went out against 49 planned slots, covering 24 distinct plan days. The Week6 sheet tab again records 0 posted and 0 post URLs, so once more the sheet says nothing happened and the world says otherwise.

The finding worth acting on

  • Sujith: Founding Product Designer, 08-25, 320 reactions and 33 comments. Not on the plan.

That was the highest-engagement post any KAM produced last week, four times his next best, and it was not one of his seven planned slots. It is a real role from his own Airtable book with 135 reachouts, and it is in this week’s pool. Two readings, not exclusive: the ranking missed a strong role, and a KAM writes with more conviction about one they picked themselves.

Both of the week’s standouts led with the constraint or the number in the first line: “₹30-40 LPA plus equity, for a company’s first ever design hire” (320 reactions) and “Remote, anywhere in India” (91 reactions). Neither buried the offer.

Caveats

Reaction counts are a snapshot taken on 31 Aug, so the Monday posts had only hours to accumulate. Public counts only; impressions need profile-owner access. Rahul republished the same Software Engineer copy on 26 and 28 Aug, counted as two posts and one distinct role. Pranav’s 31 Aug post opens “Yesterday I posted a Tech Lead role”, but no such post is in the scrape, so day 6 is counted as not posted. No applicant lift is claimed: with no post URLs in the sheet there is no clean treatment and control split, and attributing applicants without one is what produced the wrong conclusion two weeks ago.

Changed this week: every day is a distinct role, no repeated angles. Where a KAM ran short of live roles, the gap is filled with an OLDER, more senior role from that same KAM’s own Airtable book rather than a second angle on a role already used. The graphic framing line now reads “Looking for”. 19 of the 75 job pages checked had gone dead, which is why several books needed topping up. One role was dropped for an implausible published band (a ₹2-5 LPA Engagement Manager). Note: nothing was logged as posted last week, so no engagement could be measured.
Voice: curious. Notices an odd detail in the role and follows it.

Engagement and applicant impact

No engagement data is collectable for this week. The Week5 tracker tab holds all 63 planned rows, but 0 are marked Posted and 0 carry a LinkedIn post URL. Per the runbook, with no post URLs and nothing marked posted, per-post reactions, comments and reposts cannot be read, and the posted versus not-posted control group cannot be built because there is no treatment group. Either the posts did not go out, or they went out and were never logged; the sheet alone cannot tell us which. Week2 shows the same blank pattern, so logging drop-off has precedent. If the post URLs surface later, engagement can be scraped retroactively.

Applicant volumes, context only, NOT attributable to posting

DIRECT applicants on the 51 JDs featured this week, posting week against the 7 days prior. Because nothing was posted, none of this movement can be credited to LinkedIn. 46 of the 51 JDs saw any applicants.

GroupPrior week (Aug 11-17)Week of Aug 18-24Change
All featured JDs2991644+449.8%
Excluding the three outlier JDs281330+17.4%

The headline number is carried almost entirely by three JDs, which together account for 1314 of the 1644 applicants:

JDPrior weekWeek of Aug 18-24
director of engineering7603
software engineer 38506
vp engineering3205

A 7 to 603 jump on a single JD in a week with zero LinkedIn posts is a distribution event from some other channel, and is worth chasing separately. Strip those three and the rest of the book moved +17.4%, which is ordinary drift.

Changed this week: the job link is back in the FIRST COMMENT, not the post body, because putting it in the body underperformed last week. Every post now has its own graphic, linked on each card. Aditi is not posting, so this week runs 9 KAMs and 63 posts instead of 70. Two roles were dropped because the platform published an implausible salary band (a ₹2-5 LPA Engagement Manager and a ₹10-100 LPA support role), rather than repeat a figure that is almost certainly wrong.

Correction, added 25 Aug 2026

The finding above is wrong and is kept only as the historical record. It concluded that no engagement was collectable and that the applicant spikes came from some other channel. Both conclusions followed from the empty tracker, not from reality. Scraping the account managers’ own LinkedIn profiles shows they did post; the sheet was simply never filled in.

Across the seven KAMs whose profiles could be identified, 25 hiring posts went out between 18 and 24 August against 49 planned slots, a 51% fill rate, drawing 1681 reactions and 120 comments. Kritika and Raghav have no resolvable profile, so their 14 planned slots are excluded and remain unverified.

KAMPlannedPostedFillReactionsCommentsAvgBest
Tanvi7571%1492.87
Rahul7571%116923.288
Lavanya7571%1993.86
Supriya7571%151887303.6732
Priya7229%1336.512
Sujith7114%010.00
Pranav7229%120.51
Total492551%168112067.2732

The three applicant spikes are now explained. Each maps to one of Supriya’s posts: Director of Engineering, 7 to 603 applicants, posted 19 Aug with 732 reactions; Software/ML Engineer, 8 to 506, posted 22 Aug with 483 reactions; VP Engineering, 3 to 205, posted 21 Aug with 226 reactions. The applicant lift is attributable to LinkedIn after all, but it sits almost entirely with one person: Supriya accounts for 90% of the week’s reactions. The other six averaged 8.2 reactions per post, and the median post across everyone drew 5. Five posts drew none at all.

Two of the 25 were the same copy republished a day or two later (Lavanya’s SAP role on 20 and 21 Aug, Rahul’s Lead ML Engineer on 21 and 23 Aug), so 23 distinct roles were actually promoted. Method: Apify actor harvestapi/linkedin-profile-posts, profiles derived from post URLs recorded on the Week 1, Week3 and Week4 sheet tabs. Posts were classified by reading them, not by keyword match. Reaction counts are a snapshot at scrape time.

Engagement and applicant impact

29 of 70 planned posts went live (28 distinct URLs, all 28 read successfully). Across them: 147 reactions, 15 comments, 7 reposts, averaging 5.25 reactions per post. Kritika, Raghav, Aditi recorded no posted URLs, so they have no engagement rows. A post showing a single comment is usually the poster’s own link comment.

KAMPostsReactionsCommentsRepostsAvg reactions
Tanvi6632210.5
Supriya439439.75
Sujith514102.8
Lavanya212006.0
Priya612502.0
Pranav25002.5
Rahul32320.67
Total281471575.25

Applicant impact, DIRECT applicants, per distinct JD

GroupPrior week (Aug 4-10)Posting week (Aug 11-17)Change
Roles that were posted (25 JDs)114304+166.7%
Planned but not posted (24 JDs, natural control)11884-28.8%
Posted, largest mover removed106261+146.2%
Not posted, largest mover removed10670-34.0%
Posted, mature JDs only (created on/before Aug 4)3593+165.7%
Not posted, mature JDs only9269-25.0%

Read this carefully. Unlike the Aug 4-10 week, the gap is not carried by a single JD: removing the largest mover still leaves posted at +146.2% against -34.0% for the control, and 19 of 25 posted JDs rose against 6 of 24 unposted ones. But the posted group is loaded with JDs created Aug 5-9, whose baseline week is structurally depressed, and 147 reactions across 28 posts is hard to reconcile with a three-fold applicant swing coming from LinkedIn alone. These are DIRECT applicants with no source attribution, on JDs simultaneously receiving Weekday outbound reachouts. Directionally positive, not causal.

  • A post showing exactly one comment is usually the poster's own link comment, not third-party engagement.
  • Many Week4 JDs were created mid-baseline-week (Aug 2-9), so their Aug 4-10 baseline is structurally depressed and week-on-week growth is overstated. A mature-JD-only cut (created on/before Aug 4) is given in the summary.
  • The posting-week applicant window is truncated at run time (Mon 17 Aug morning), so it is not a full 7 days.
  • Rows with no post are counted at JD level: several rows share one JD (e.g. Supriya's 7 WarpBuild angles = 1 JD), so applicant maths is done per distinct JD, never per row.
  • Sujith Day 2 (Richpanel AE Outbound) and Day 6 (Richpanel AE Inbound) carry the SAME LinkedIn URL. One post, two rows, two different JDs. The Outbound JD may never have been posted.
  • Rahul's Day 2, 3 and 5 rows carry post URLs whose slug text names a different role than the row (VectorShift PM row -> 'frontend-architect' post, Ema Backend row -> 'hiring-for-frontend' post, Eudia Frontend Architect row -> 'hiring-for-software' post). The row-to-post mapping for Rahul is unreliable.
  • Tanvi Day 3 (Genios AI) is marked Posted=No in the sheet but carries a live post URL with 9 reactions. It is treated as posted (runbook v6(b): a real post URL is proof of posting).
  • Tanvi Day 6 held a shortened lnkd.in link; it resolves to share urn 7493039781971382275 on Tanvi's profile.
  • Reaction/comment/repost counts of 0 mean the post rendered with no count shown. Only genuinely unreachable posts are null.
  • Applicants are inboundType='DIRECT' on the JD. They are NOT attributed to LinkedIn; Weekday's own outbound reachouts run on the same JDs in the same week, and newly created JDs ramp naturally. No source attribution exists in this data, so causation cannot be established.
  • The not-posted group is not a randomised control. It is dominated by three KAMs (Kritika, Raghav, Aditi) who posted nothing at all, so KAM-level and role-mix differences are confounded with posting.

Engagement and applicant impact

33 of 70 planned posts went live (32 distinct URLs, all read successfully). Across them: 362 reactions, 88 comments, 2 reposts, averaging 11.3 reactions per post. Kritika, Supriya, Raghav and Aditi recorded no posted URLs, so they have no engagement rows.

Applicant impact, DIRECT applicants

GroupPrior week (Jul 28-Aug 3)Posting week (Aug 4-10)Change
Roles that were posted (27 JDs)239295+23.4%
Planned but not posted (35 JDs, natural control)179126-29.6%
Posted, excluding one outlier JD232145-37.5%

Read this carefully. The whole headline lift sits in one JD (Pranav Day 2, Fullstack Engineer): 7 applicants the week before, 150 in the posting week. That post drew 2 reactions and 1 comment, so the spike almost certainly did not come from LinkedIn. Strip it out and posted roles fell 37.5% while unposted roles fell 29.6%. On this week of evidence the posts did not produce a measurable applicant lift.

  • The posting week window is truncated: applicant data ends 2026-08-10 04:00 UTC, so roughly 6.2 of 7 days are counted. This understates the posting week for both groups equally.
  • Only 33 of 70 planned posts were actually posted, and 4 of 10 KAMs posted nothing, so this is a partial-compliance week.
  • The unposted rows are a natural control group but not a randomised one: unposted roles were often skipped for a reason, including a LinkedIn ban on one account and an instruction not to post one client.
  • JDs created mid-window depress the prior-week baseline.
  • Both windows are 7 days and non-overlapping.
  • Engagement counts are a point-in-time read on 2026-08-10 and will keep accruing for the most recent posts.
Voice: curious. Asks the plain question everyone is thinking, then answers it.
